If you were to take a city bus instead of driving your petrol hatchback (<1400cc) for 12 km, you would hypothetically avoid 1.378 kg of CO2 emissions per trip.

This is based on a provisional estimate of 1.56 kg CO2 for the 12 km car ride [S1] and 0.182 kg CO2 for the 12 km bus ride [S2]. Both estimates are for tank-to-wheel CO2 only. The bus factor is per passenger-km, based on the State Transport Utility fleet average load [S2].

If you were to take a city bus instead of driving your petrol sedan (<1400cc) for 20 km, you would hypothetically avoid 2.537 kg of CO2 emissions per trip.

This is calculated by comparing the estimated emissions of a 20 km car ride in a petrol sedan (2.84 kg CO2 [S1]) with a 20 km bus ride (0.303 kg CO2 [S2]).

The emission factor for the petrol sedan is 0.142 kg CO2 per vehicle-km [S1], and for the bus, it is 0.015161 kg CO2 per passenger-km [S2]. Both factors are provisional [S1, S2] and are based on 2015 data, rated efficiency, and only account for tank-to-wheel CO2 emissions [S1, S2].

You would hypothetically avoid 0.81 kg of CO2 per 15 km trip by taking a small CNG car instead of your diesel hatchback (<1400cc). This is a hypothetical comparison.

The provisional emission factor for a diesel hatchback (<1400cc) is 0.117 kg CO2 per vehicle-km [S1], and for a small CNG car, it is 0.063 kg CO2 per vehicle-km [S2]. These factors are for CO2 only and represent tank-to-wheel emissions based on the 2015 fleet and rated efficiency [S1, S2].
